title: implement AdamW

atoms.evidence: self.m = [t.zeros_like(p) for p in self.params]; self.v = [t.zeros_like(p) for p in self.params]
for p in self.params: p.grad = None
theta *= 1 - self.lr * self.lmda  (decoupled WD inplace) and theta -= self.lr * m_hat / (v_hat.sqrt() + self.eps) (main update inplace)
m.copy_(self.beta1 * m + (1 - self.beta1) * g); v.copy_(self.beta2 * v + (1 - self.beta2) * g.pow(2))

theta *= 1 - self.lr * self.lmda — applied directly to theta BEFORE the gradient-based update, not folded into g; this IS the defining change vs Adam (markdown: 'This is a very small modification of the Adam update rule, where we apply weight decay in a different way (by modifying the weights themselves...)')
m_hat = m / (1 - self.beta1**self.t); v_hat = v / (1 - self.beta2**self.t)
Markdown gives 8-line LaTeX pseudocode for AdamW; differs from Adam only in placement of weight-decay line
f'AdamW(lr={self.lr}, beta1={self.beta1}, beta2={self.beta2}, eps={self.eps}, weight_decay={self.lmda})' — provided in template

atoms_in_seed_but_not_actually_present.reason: Seed predicted this for AdamW but the whole point of AdamW is that it DOESN'T use L2-style g += lambda*theta; it uses decoupled decay instead. The Adam-style L2 fold is replaced by weight-decay-decoupled.
Solution applies theta *= 1 - lr*lmda unconditionally (lmda=0 makes it a no-op). No 'if lmda != 0' branch as in SGD/RMSprop/Adam solutions.

notes: 15 atoms tagged + 2 false positives flagged. 1 below seed prediction of 11+conditional. AdamW = Adam's atom set minus weight-decay-l2-add plus weight-decay-decoupled; the solution drops the conditional shortcut on weight decay too (multiplies by 1 unconditionally when lmda=0). The decoupled WD line BEFORE the m/v EMA updates is the conceptual content the exercise tests.
